qti-assessment-test.title: National Academy of Continuing Legal Education - E-Discovery FRE 502(d) & ABA Tech Ethics CLE (Demo)

qti-assessment-item.title: Draft Federal Rule of Evidence 502(d) non-waiver orders and proportional FRCP Rule 26(f) ESI protocols to protect privilege during high-volume productions.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_1): Draft Federal Rule of Evidence 502(d) non-waiver orders and proportional FRCP Rule 26(f) ESI protocols to protect privilege during high-volume productions.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Litigation counsel faces a compressed rolling production of 450,000 Slack messages and emails in federal court. Why should counsel move for a court-entered FRE 502(d) order rather than relying solely on FRE 502(b) or an unentered FRE 502(e) stipulation?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: A court-entered FRE 502(d) order prevents privilege waiver in both the pending federal action and any other federal or state proceeding without litigating FRE 502(b) 'reasonable steps' adequacy
An unentered FRE 502(e) party letter automatically binds third-party subpoenas in subsequent state-court class actions
FRE 502(d) allows counsel to intentionally use privileged documents offensively as a sword while shielding related communications
FRE 502(b) eliminates any obligation to rectify an inadvertent disclosure once counsel discovers it

qti-content-body.p: Verified: FRE 502(d) provides nationwide federal and state non-waiver protection against third parties without costly post-production 'reasonable steps' motion practice.
Diagnostic rationale: Under FRE 502(e), a bilateral party agreement binds only the signatories unless incorporated into a court order under FRE 502(d).

Diagnostic rationale: Selective offensive use of privileged material triggers subject-matter waiver principles; FRE 502(d) protects against unintended disclosure waiver, not selective sword-and-shield abuse.
Diagnostic rationale: FRE 502(b)(3) expressly requires prompt reasonable steps to rectify the error once known.

qti-assessment-item.title: Apply FRCP Rule 37(e) preservation duties and curative versus intent-to-deprive spoliation standards to ephemeral messaging and cloud repositories.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_2): Apply FRCP Rule 37(e) preservation duties and curative versus intent-to-deprive spoliation standards to ephemeral messaging and cloud repositories.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: After receiving a credible pre-suit demand letter, a corporate defendant issues a written email hold but negligently forgets to pause a 14-day auto-purge setting on an executive messaging channel, without any intent to hide evidence. Under FRCP Rule 37(e), which sanction is permissible if prejudice is shown?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Mandatory jury instruction presuming the lost messages were unfavorable to the defendant under Rule 37(e)(2)
Targeted curative measures no greater than necessary to cure the prejudice under Rule 37(e)(1), excluding adverse-inference instructions or dismissal
Automatic default judgment on liability regardless of alternative evidence

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: Rule 37(e)(2) restricts adverse-inference jury instructions, dismissal, and default judgment strictly to cases where the party acted with 'intent to deprive'.
Verified: Negligent or even grossly negligent failure to suspend auto-delete without intent to deprive is governed by Rule 37(e)(1) proportional curative remedies.
Diagnostic rationale: Default judgment requires an affirmative finding of intent to deprive under Rule 37(e)(2)(C).
Diagnostic rationale: Rule 11 governs signed pleadings/motions, not ESI preservation.

qti-assessment-item.title: Implement ABA Model Rules 1.1 (Comment 8), 1.6(c), 3.3, and 5.3 supervisory controls when using generative AI or cloud legal-tech vendors.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_3): Implement ABA Model Rules 1.1 (Comment 8), 1.6(c), 3.3, and 5.3 supervisory controls when using generative AI or cloud legal-tech vendors.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: An associate pastes an unredacted M&A due-diligence memo into a consumer generative AI web tool whose terms permit human contractor review and model training, then files the AI-drafted brief without cite-checking two fabricated appellate holdings. Which ABA Model Rules were violated?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Only Model Rule 1.5 on fee reasonableness, provided the associate did not bill for the prompt time
Model Rules 1.1 (technological competence), 1.6(c) (confidentiality), and 3.3(a)(1) (candor toward the tribunal)
Zero ethical rules because software vendors bear sole strict liability for citation accuracy
Model Rule 4.2 on communicating with represented parties

qti-content-body.p: Diagnostic rationale: While ABA Formal Opinion 512 also addresses billing transparency under Rule 1.5, the primary breaches here are competence, confidentiality, and candor.
Verified: Exposing client confidences to a training-enabled tool violates Rules 1.1 & 1.6(c), and filing unverified fabricated case citations violates Rule 3.3(a)(1).
Diagnostic rationale: Signing and filing counsel hold non-delegable duties under FRCP Rule 11 and Model Rule 3.3.
Diagnostic rationale: Rule 4.2 governs ex parte contact with represented persons, not AI vendor confidentiality or brief verification.

qti-assessment-item.title: Implement ABA Model Rules 1.1 (Comment 8), 1.6(c), 3.3, and 5.3 supervisory controls when using generative AI or cloud legal-tech vendors.

qti-item-body.p: Objective (OBJ_3): Implement ABA Model Rules 1.1 (Comment 8), 1.6(c), 3.3, and 5.3 supervisory controls when using generative AI or cloud legal-tech vendors.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: Under ABA Model Rule 5.3 and Formal Opinion 512, which firm governance control is required before deploying a cloud e-discovery or legal-AI platform across client matters?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: Verify zero-training contractual data isolation, encryption/access controls, and mandatory lawyer primary-source verification prior to any external filing
Allow individual paralegals to adopt free browser extensions ad hoc without IT or ethics review
Delegate final brief sign-off to the cloud vendor's automated confidence score
Disclose opposing counsel's privileged clawback documents into public prompt libraries

qti-content-body.p: Verified: Rule 5.3 requires vetting third-party technology terms (confidentiality, zero model-training retention, security) and enforcing lawyer review of outputs.
Diagnostic rationale: Unvetted shadow-IT extensions create direct Rule 1.6 confidentiality breaches.
Diagnostic rationale: Independent professional judgment and Rule 3.3 verification can never be delegated to software confidence scores.
Diagnostic rationale: Uploading clawed-back or confidential discovery materials to public systems violates protective orders and ethics rules.
